look_here_first: Start with ray color. Maroon blanketflower is an annual with leafy branching stems and heads carrying dark maroon-red to purple rays, usually without the bright yellow tips common in G. pulchella.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: annual; taprooted; leafy branching stems; alternate oblanceolate to spatulate leaves; dark red to maroon or purple rays; ray tips 3-lobed; disk florets yellow to dark red with purple tips; open sandy or rocky sites

key_traits.label: Comparison training
key_traits.text: G. pulchella usually has conspicuous yellow-tipped red rays; G. amblyodon is much more uniformly maroon/red. G. suavis is perennial and scapose with rays often reduced or absent.
